items.title: Steve Buckingham, interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 25, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Oh they sang with everybody. Elvis, Ricky Nelson, everybody.

ctx.x: Oh they sang with everybody. Elvis, Ricky Nelson, everybody. But they developed that thing where they would listen to a tune, a demo, and the lyric sheet would be in it, and over every note they would write 1, 4, 6 minor, which in the key of C you’re talking about C, 4 would be F, 6 minor would be A minor, it’s all relative. Everybody, every studio musician, if they didn’t have perfect pitch they had perfect relative pitch. You give them the root note and hit the next and they’ll tell you if it’s a 3, 4, 5, 6…
How did you divide the work up, because usually you had multiple guitar players on a session?

items.title: Buckingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2019
items.q: Elvis certainly didn’t come from an affluent background.

ctx.x: Good answer. I’m not sure I can verbalize this question, but sometimes I read sociologists writing about music and then you read musicians talking about where their music came from. And a lot of times they’re not sort of on the same page. I wonder how much you feel the social conditions that musicians grow up in affects their musicianship.

Good question. Well if you look at the greats, the legends, they certainly didn’t come from affluent background. Louis Armstrong certainly didn’t. Hank Williams certainly didn’t. I think you go to any great legendary musician and it usually comes — I mean Dolly, very humble backgrounds. You’re talking about I mean really humble backgrounds, and a lot of these people, whether it’s country, blues, jazz, rock & roll, Elvis certainly didn’t come from an affluent background. He was influenced by Chuck Berry and Fats…

least this is the way it used to be. Now, somebody told me today, one of the students said something to me about — I was talking about the recording and how it used to be, the studios. A student said, “Yeah but it might be more democratized now because everybody can make a record.” And I said, “You’re right. Everybody who has a laptop can put on garage band and make a record.
